about: The standing committees a legislative body refers bills to, by the subject of a bill's first section. Each committee lists the catalog topics (the part after 'us-policy-positions:'), law series and budget lines it hears. A body no larger than the committee-of-the-whole size hears every bill as a whole. Each chamber's own committee names are not in the data yet (SG-GOV-committee-names-national).
source: The subjects nearly every state chamber keeps a standing committee for: appropriations or finance, judiciary, education, health and human services, labor and commerce, transportation, natural resources and environment, state and local government, and housing (Book of the States 2023, Table 3.23; NCSL, 'Legislative Committee Structures', 2024; Congress's House and Senate standing committees divide the same subjects). Spread: chambers keep 10 to 40 committees; the game keeps one per subject.
